title: Morning Edition
dek: Djibouti's migrant-boat disaster; emergency rule in Pakistan; Hurricane Simon; Korean missile tests; and a small Italian chestnut festival.

lead_story.headline: Djibouti boat disaster kills at least 139 migrants
lead_story.summary: A boat with 305 people aboard sank off Obock on October 8–9. By October 11 the IOM and local authorities reported 139 dead, 84 missing and 82 survivors; searches continued.
lead_story.why_it_matters: A perilous route to Yemen and Gulf employment remains heavily used despite the region's conflicts.

items.headline: Pakistan places Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under emergency rule
items.summary: President Zardari approved an emergency and governor's rule on October 11 in the opposition-led province. The federal government cites militancy; PTI disputes the takeover.
items.why_it_matters: Security measures and constitutional federalism are colliding with democratic representation.

items.headline: Hurricane Simon threatens Mexico's Pacific coast
items.summary: Jalisco issued red alerts and closed some activities as Simon passed close to shore. A late October 11 NHC advisory located it offshore with 105-knot winds; dangerous rain and surf continued.
items.why_it_matters: Flooding and landslides may be severe even when a hurricane weakens.

items.headline: North Korea fires multiple ballistic missiles
items.summary: South Korea reported multiple October 12 launches near Pyongyang, with at least one missile traveling over 900 kilometers, after recent military tests on both sides.
items.why_it_matters: Reciprocal weapons demonstrations heighten tension and miscalculation risk.

items.headline: Brazilian state declares emergency as wildfire smoke closes schools
items.summary: Smoke in Manaus prompted school closures; on October 11 Amazonas reported emergency recognition for 36 municipalities affected by fires.
items.why_it_matters: Air pollution turns environmental emergencies into public-health and education disruptions.

items.headline: Older catch-up: climate hazards disrupted school for 171 million students
items.summary: A September UNICEF analysis found at least 171 million students experienced climate-related school interruptions in 2025 across 106 countries and territories.
items.why_it_matters: The long-term cost of extreme weather includes lost learning, especially in lower-income countries.

items.headline: Webb traces the most distant known fast radio burst
items.summary: A MeerKAT radio flash was linked with Webb observations to a small galaxy at redshift 2.148, when the universe was roughly three billion years old.
items.why_it_matters: Distant bursts can probe otherwise unseen cosmic gas; their engines remain uncertain.

items.headline: A village's chestnut weekend in Italy
items.summary: Grancia di Morino scheduled its 28th chestnut festival for October 9–11, with food stalls, music, workshops and a waterfall walk.
items.why_it_matters: An ordinary harvest gives neighbors a reason to share craft, landscape and time.

items.headline: What if moral conflict means choosing between good things?
items.summary: Irene McMullin argues that our projects, duties to particular people and obligations to society can make equally legitimate but incompatible demands.
items.why_it_matters: Ethics sometimes requires practical judgment rather than a single rule or a fight against selfishness.

worth_your_time.headline: How the parenthesis became a Renaissance literary art
worth_your_time.summary: Florence Hazrat uses Philip Sidney's Arcadia to show how punctuation, interruption and digression shape literary voice.
worth_your_time.why_it_matters: An overlooked typographic detail becomes a way to understand how writing thinks.
